ideas.reasoning: I favor A over restarting: evaluation of the complete, symmetrically retained blocks offers the most information per additional episode, with no training or controller-generation calls. It would test whether reward-trained corrections transfer to deterministic sustained success rather than merely improving training diagnostics. Its weakest points are the explicit frozen stopping rule and only two training blocks, so this requires a user-authorized amendment and supports conclusions about these finalists only.

question: R-103 stopped INCOMPLETE under its own hard ceiling, exactly as agreed. Facts. The rerun smoke on seed 4770 passed all seven gates (512 episodes started). Blocks 0 and 1 completed all three arms at exactly 460,800 transitions each. Block 2's first run (draws) was stopped by the child's allowance at 230,272 transitions; block 2 ARS and PPO never started; no selection or fresh evaluation cell has run, so no sustained-success outcome of any trained policy exists. Cause: my episode estimate was wrong, not the simulator. In the draws and ARS runs each generation is a forced full reset (128 starts) followed by 360 steps whose final step time-outs every surviving environment, and Isaac auto-resets those (about 128 more starts that are then discarded by the next forced reset). Those are real 'episodes started' under the agreed counting rule, so a draws/ARS run starts about 2,563 episodes, not about 1,330; PPO starts 1,435. Episodes started so far: 15,430 (514 first smoke + 512 smoke + 13,123 in six complete runs + 1,281 in the cut run). The full protocol would have needed about 25,300. Training diagnostics only (reward and per-step predicate fraction, stochastic for PPO, not success evidence): PPO's mean step reward rose 0.320 -> 0.352 (block 0) and 0.334 -> 0.385 (block 1), predicate fraction 0.47 -> 0.55 and 0.48 -> 0.59, critic explained variance 0.87-0.91, KL at target, coefficients reached the 0.10 bound; ARS's population mean score is flat (110-135) with theta at the bound from iteration 5; draws' best training scores are 167 and 159 with small theta (max |theta| 0.022, 0.033). Options. (A) Evaluate the two complete blocks only, as a declared deviation: selection (reference + 15 checkpoints on 64 cases) and fresh (reference + 3 finalists on 128 cases) for blocks 0 and 1 = at most 3,072 episodes, total at most 18,502 <= 20,000; the reduction from three blocks to two was forced mechanically by the ceiling before any evaluation outcome existed and is symmetric across arms; the primary would be judged on 256 case pairs with the same rules, the block-level interval would have 1 degree of freedom and no learner-level claim would be possible; block 2's partial draws run is discarded and seeds 4762, 4766, 4769 are reported as spent/unused. (B) Close R-103 now as inconclusive with no evaluation, and propose a new preregistered idea with new seeds and corrected accounting. (C) something else you prefer. My own view: (A) is within the ceiling and the reserved evaluation allowance, spends nothing on training, changes no frozen setting, and the selection of which blocks to evaluate did not depend on any outcome; the agreed text, however, says the protocol 'stops with an incomplete result', so I will not run it without agreement. Which do you want, and does it need the user's decision?
